predecessors.name: Western Chalukya Empire
predecessors.text: Kalyani and the northern Deccan, taken in c.

successors.name: Khalji dynasty
successors.text: the whole kingdom, annexed by the Khalji sultanate (Malik Kafur 1313, Mubarak Shah 1317)

ledger.x: c. 1187: Bhillama V founds the Yadava kingdom of Devagiri. 'Around 1187, Bhillama forced Ballala to retreat, conquered the former Chalukya capital Kalyani'; 'He then established Devagiri, a formidable natural stronghold, which became the new Yadava capital.' The infobox says 'Established: c. 1187'. Cliopatria's row…

c. 1187: Bhillama V takes Kalyani from the Western Chalukyas ('conquered the former Chalukya capital Kalyani'). The page describes no battle against the Chalukya armies; the western-chalukya-empire dossier records the matching 1187 loss.
late 1180s: the Hoysalas push the Yadavas north.

c. 1191: the Hoysalas win at Soratur and Lakkundi and hold the land north to the Malaprabha and Krishna. 'In c. 1191, the Hoysala monarch gained the upper hand over Yadava Bhillama V in the critical battles of Soratur and Lakkundi' (Veera Ballala II page); 'By c. 1189, Basavakalyana had fallen to Bhillama V'. The…

c. 1194: the Yadava Jaitugi invades the Kakatiya country. The Seuna page: Jaitugi invaded around 1194 and forced them to accept Yadava suzerainty. The front is not named, so the zone is the frontier band.
1198: the Yadavas install Ganapati as a vassal.
1198: Jaitugi makes Ganapati his vassal.
1212: Singhana II takes the land north of the Tungabhadra from the Hoysalas.
1216: Singhana II annexes the Kolhapur kingdom.
1220: the Yadava general Kholeshvara invades Lata.
1220: Lata is given to Shankha as a Yadava vassal.

c. 1231: Ganapati becomes independent. 'During the second half of his reign, Ganapati seems to have assumed an independent status' and the page records no major conflict between the two kings or any date for the change. Ganapati reigned c. 1199-1262, so the middle of the reign, 1231, is a bridge (page silent…
c. 1232: peace with the Chaulukyas. 'The Chaulukya-Yadava conflict came to end in c. 1232 with a peace treaty.' The page adds that Lata was later lost to Lavanaprasada's invasion (undated).
c. 1232: Shankha's Lata passes out of Yadava hands. The page dates the loss to Lavanaprasada's invasion only as 'later'; the 1232 peace is the bridge (page silent; confidence 1).

c. 1265: the Yadavas take the northern Konkan. The Shilahara dynasty page lists the North Konkan Shilaharas as 'c. 800-1265 CE', capital Thane, the last ruler Someshvara 1255-1265, 'subdued by the Yadava ruler Singhana II around the beginning of the 13th century'; the Seuna page has Mahadeva (r. c. 1261-1270) curb 'a…
1294: the Kakatiyas take Raichur.
1296: Alauddin Khalji, governor of Kara, raids Devagiri.
1296: the raid ends with a ransom and annual tribute.
1307: Alauddin sends Malik Kafur against Devagiri.
1308: Ramachandra submits.
1271-1308: Ramachandra extends the kingdom to the north-east.
1313: Malik Kafur annexes Devagiri.

c. 1316: Harapaladeva restores Yadava rule at Devagiri. The page has the Yadavas seize Devagiri and declare independence, led by Harapaladeva and his minister Raghava. It gives no date for the rebellion; Kafur left in 1315 and died in February 1316, so 1316 is a bridge (page silent; confidence 1). The Seuna page lists…
April 1317: Mubarak Shah marches on Devagiri.
1317: Harapaladeva is captured after two or three skirmishes and beheaded: 'Harapaladeva was presented before Mubarak Shah, who ordered his beheading.'
1317: Devagiri passes to Delhi for good.
1317: the Yadava dynasty ends at Devagiri; the Seuna page has it 'annexed by the Khalji sultanate in 1317'.

wars.name: Seuna conquest of Kalyani
wars.outcome: Bhillama V conquered the former Chalukya capital Kalyani and founded Devagiri.

wars.name: Hoysala victory at Soratur
wars.outcome: Ballala's Hoysalas decisively defeated Bhillama at Soratur and pushed the Yadavas north of the Malaprabha and Krishna.

wars.name: Jaitugi's Kakatiya war
wars.outcome: Jaitugi invaded about 1194 and forced Yadava suzerainty; in 1198 Mahadeva was killed and Ganapati installed as a Yadava vassal (Singhana II page).

wars.name: Singhana II's conquest of the northern Hoysala land
wars.outcome: By 1212 the Yadavas had reached Anantapur, Bellary, Chitradurga and Shimoga; by 1213 most of Dharwad; the conquest north of the Tungabhadra was completed by 1220 (the Hoysala page of the hoysala-kingdom dossier says after c.

wars.name: Yadava invasion of Malwa
wars.outcome: Simhana II invaded in 1215 and defeated Arjunavarman; Krishna defeated the Paramara king before 1250 and Ramachandra defeated the Paramara army in the 1270s; no annexation is recorded.

wars.name: Conquest of the Kolhapur Shilaharas
wars.outcome: Simhana II defeated Bhoja II, who fled to Panhala; the kingdom including Kolhapur was annexed about 1216.

wars.name: Yadava invasions of Lata
wars.outcome: Kholeshvara captured Lata in 1220 and Shankha ruled it as a Yadava vassal; a joint invasion with Paramara Devapala failed; peace about 1232; Visaladeva's invasion of Gujarat in the 1240s failed.

wars.name: Mahadeva's invasion of the Kakatiya kingdom
wars.outcome: Mahadeva invaded the eastern Kakatiya kingdom and was apparently repulsed; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Ramachandra's northern wars
wars.outcome: Ramachandra defeated the Paramara army in the 1270s, fought the Vaghelas inconclusively (the Thane and Cintra inscriptions each claim a win), occupied Tripuri (undated) and subdued Vajrakara and Bhandagara (undated); a Varanasi temple suggests he held the…

wars.name: Yadava-Hoysala war of 1275-1276
wars.outcome: Tikkama invaded in autumn 1275; the Hoysala forces were defeated in January 1276; on 25 April 1276 Ankeya Nayaka led a decisive attack and Tikkama retreated to Dhummi; no border moved.

wars.name: Kakatiya conquest of the Raichur Doab
wars.outcome: Vitthala-deva-nayaka fortified Raichur in 1294; after 1296 Prataparudra annexed the eastern part of Ramachandra's kingdom, including the Anantapur and Raichur districts.

wars.name: Khalji conquest of Devagiri
wars.outcome: Alauddin raided Devagiri in 1296 for ransom and tribute; Malik Kafur subjugated Ramachandra in 1307-1308; after Simhana III's revolt Kafur annexed Devagiri in 1313; Harapaladeva restored Yadava rule until Mubarak Shah's campaign of April 1317 ended it.

certainty.note: Yadava frontiers rest on inscription find-spots and claims; no treaty line is recorded.
